page.layout: One page of text: a Latin poem in italic type, followed below by a dedication in capitals. Running head at the top. No page number is printed.

p.i: VRsinum dederas unum, Deus Optime, nobis, Sufficeret nobis tua qui pene omnia solus. Siue homines ille humana ratione doceret, Artibus excultus cunctis: siue entheus illum Spiritus arcanos depromere pectore sensus Iusserat, & sacri quatientem lampada verbi, Discutere errorum nebulas, cuneosque ruentum Diuinis fretum telis hinc inde luporum Rumpere, tutantem Christi diuinitus agnos.
Ergo quid Vrsino properata morte perempto, Crediderim superesse gregi, qui sicut in uno Cuncta habuit quondam, sic cuncta amisit in uno?
Sic ego multa gemens, & planctib. aera complens Quum Deus excelsa miseratus ab arce gementem, Pone modum lachrimis, inquit, vobisque, sibique Vivit, qui vitam impendit vobisque, mihique.
Ergo, Vrsine, abfit nobisque, tibique, Deoque, Vt te viventem deinceps ceu lumine cassum Ploremus stulti, quem tot tantique labores Aeternum aeterna consecravere saluti.

Et quibus hosce lupos tecum victricibus armis Fregimus, in media nobis quum morte relinquas, Nempe etiam nobis vere post funera vivis: Et vives donec coelorum regia tecum Felici excipiat functos certamine cunctos.

main_text.head: ZACHARIAE VRSINO SILESIO, VIRO IN OMNI DISCIPLINARUM GENERE EXERCITATISSIMO, THEOLOGO SUMMO, VITAE INCULPATAE, IUDICIO ADMIRABILI, LABORE INDEFESSO, TH. BEZA CHARISSIMO IN CHRISTO FRATRI, P.[?]

page.notes: The word "P." at the end of the dedication is followed by a small mark that I could not identify with confidence. The initial V of the poem is a large decorative letter joined to "Rsinum". Two words in the poem are underlined or marked by a small sign, but the marks do not change the text. The spacing in "vere post funera" is tight in the scan. Several u/v and i/j forms were normalised as instructed (for example "unum", "viuit" as "vivit", "Iusserat" as "Iusserat" with I kept as the printed initial letter).
